title: Surface room & bed number alongside tenant identity everywhere
description: Room.roomNumber already exists at the schema/property-setup level, but wardens think of tenants by room number first, name second - the reverse of how the app currently presents them. Tenant list rows, tenant profile, invoices, payment records, and reminder previews all show name/phone with no room reference. Surface 'Room 204 - Bed B' (or equivalent) next to the tenant's name everywhere a tenant is identified.
acceptanceCriteria: Tenant directory list rows show each tenant's current room+bed alongside their name
Tenant profile screen shows room+bed prominently near the top
Invoice list rows and the payment recording screen show room+bed, not just tenant name
A vacated tenant's historical room+bed still displays (not blanked out after checkout)

history.note: Added from the v2 feedback session (warden interviews after the v1 field test) and from buried enhancement/limitation notes surfaced while re-reading the full v1 board history.

Starting - adding a shared bed-location lookup (beds JOIN rooms) so room+bed can be surfaced on the tenant directory, tenant profile, invoice list and record-payment screens. Using the tenant's latest agreement (active if any, else most recent closed) so a vacated tenant keeps showing their historical room+bed per AC 4.

Room+bed now travels with tenant identity everywhere. Added data/dao/BedLocation.kt (roomNumber + bedLabel) resolved in one beds-JOIN-rooms query via BedDao.getLocation/BedRepository.getLocation, and TenancyAgreementDao.getLatestByTenantId (ORDER BY status = 'ACTIVE' DESC, moveInDate DESC) so a vacated tenant still resolves to the bed they last occupied - that's AC 4. Shared ui/common/BedLocationLabel.kt renders it as the single 'Room 204 - Bed B' string (R.string.bed_location, en + hi) so no screen formats it itself. Consumers: TenantDirectoryScreen rows (location above the name, primary colour), TenantProfileScreen (directly under the name near the top), InvoiceListScreen rows, and RecordPaymentScreen's invoice header. Tests: TenantDirectoryViewModelTest and TenantProfileViewModelTest gained location cases (including closed-agreement and no-agreement-at-all); InvoiceListViewModelTest and RecordPaymentViewModelTest assert the enriched location. gradlew testDebugUnitTest green.

FAIL on AC1 and AC2 - the room+bed label is rendered, but it is stale: it shows the wrong value, or nothing at all, until the ViewModel happens to be recreated. AC3 and AC4 pass and are genuinely good: invoice rows and the Record Payment screen both show 'Room 102 - Bed A', and after checkout the vacated tenant still shows their historical room+bed with a VACATED badge rather than being blanked. THE BUG, two reproductions. (1) Onboard a tenant: the directory row shows name and phone but NO room+bed at all; force-stop and relaunch and 'Room 101 - Bed A' appears. (2) With that tenant in Room 101 Bed A, transfer them to Room 102 Bed A: the transfer is correct in the DB, but the tenant profile still reads 'Room 101 - Bed A' on return, and the directory row still reads 'Room 101 - Bed A' too. Both correct themselves only once the screen's ViewModel is recreated. ROOT CAUSE: the location is resolved once and never re-observed. TenantProfileViewModel.init (lines 42-48) does a single suspend read - getLatestByTenantId() then getLocation() - assigns _location and never refreshes, so a bedId change cannot reach it. TenantDirectoryViewModel.init recomputes items only inside tenantRepository.getAll().collect { ... locationOf(it.id) }, i.e. only when the TENANTS table emits; onboarding inserts the tenant row BEFORE the agreement is created, and a transfer touches only tenancy_agreements, so neither triggers a recompute. I confirmed the data layer is fine - the DAO join returns ('101','A') correctly and the label is right after a restart - so this is purely a refresh problem. SUGGESTED FIX: have both ViewModels observe tenancy_agreements (and beds) as Flows and derive location reactively, instead of reading it once per tenants-table emission.

Fixed - the label is now derived reactively instead of read once. TenantProfileViewModel: replaced the single `getLatestByTenantId()` read in init with a collect on `observeByTenantId(tenantId)`, resolving location and planned move-out on every emission. Also dropped the optimistic `_plannedMoveOut.value = millis` from setPlannedMoveOut so the flow is the single source of truth. TenantDirectoryViewModel: init now `combine`s the tenants flow with a new `observeAll()` agreements flow and resolves each tenant's location per emission; the now-dead private locationOf() is gone. Added TenancyAgreementDao.observeAll() + repository observeByTenantId/observeAll to back this. VERIFIED ON EMULATOR - both original repros, without any restart: (1) onboarded Suresh and 'Room 101 · Bed A' appeared on the directory row immediately, where before it was blank until relaunch; (2) transferred him to Room 102 Bed B and both the profile header and the directory row updated to 'Room 102 · Bed B' on return, where before both showed the old room. Added two regression tests to TenantDirectoryViewModelTest driving a MutableStateFlow of agreements - one for the transfer case, one for the agreement-written-after-tenant-row case - both of which fail against the old one-shot implementation. Build and full suite green: 412 tests pass (4 new), ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest and assembleDebug both successful. Tests touched for the new signatures: TenantProfileViewModelTest and TenantDirectoryViewModelTest now mock the observed agreement flows, InvoiceListViewModelTest gains the ReconciliationRepository mock, and DataPacketTest gains the noticeGiven label. Note on two profile tests: they assert state after setPlannedMoveOut, which previously passed only because the ViewModel wrote the value optimistically. Rather than keep that second source of truth - the exact bug class LODGY-33 is about - the mocks now use a MutableStateFlow that re-emits on write, which is how Room actually behaves.

PASS - both original repros fixed, and I went looking for the bug the fix could have introduced. AC1: onboarded a brand-new tenant (Suresh) and 'Room 101 · Bed A' appeared on the directory row IMMEDIATELY, where before it stayed blank until an app restart. AC2: the profile shows room+bed prominently under the name. Transfer case: moved Suresh from Room 101 Bed A to Room 102 Bed B and both the profile header and the directory row updated to the new bed on return, with no restart - previously both kept showing the old room. AC3: invoice rows and the Record Payment screen still show room+bed (verified on Priya's invoice - 'Room 501 · Bed A'). AC4: a vacated tenant still resolves to their last bed - Ramesh Kumar shows 'Room 102 · Bed A' with a VACATED badge rather than being blanked. THE RISK I CHASED: the developer replaced the DAO's SQL ordering (ORDER BY status='ACTIVE' DESC, moveInDate DESC) with a hand-written Kotlin comparator, so I tested the returning-tenant case DESIGN.md section 3 explicitly calls out. Injected a second agreement for Ramesh - ACTIVE, on Room 101 Bed A, with a move-in date EARLIER than his existing CLOSED one - which discriminates the two orderings: if status is weighed first the app must show Room 101 Bed A, if date is weighed first it would wrongly show Room 102 Bed A. Both the directory and the profile resolved to Room 101 · Bed A, so the comparator matches the SQL precedence exactly. Synthetic row removed afterwards.
